non_negotiable_invariants: Every capability reachable today stays reachable: no control, route, permission semantic, durable state transition, recovery path or error behaviour may be removed or silently altered by a UI change.

Authorization, approval, admission and sandbox semantics are server-authored; the UI renders them and never decides them. A disabled control must reflect an authoritative refusal, not a client-side guess.

Durable state and API contracts are unchanged unless the story explicitly says otherwise and a backend test proves the transition.
Untrusted text from models, repositories or tools never grants authority and never becomes markup that can execute.
Evidence over claims: screenshots, keyboard walks and test output are recorded as they happened; skipped or environment-blocked checks are reported as skipped.
One story per branch and pull request; the shared ledger is the only claim mechanism.

open_risks: The plan was authored from GitHub web extracts, not a local checkout: baseline.readme, baseline.frontend and baseline.roadmap say 'retrieved live', tests say 'not executed', and the backend API contracts were 'not fully audited'. UIUX-P0-01 to P0-06 exist to replace that with measured evidence; until they close, every current-behaviour statement in this ledger is a hypothesis.

Tab labels in this ledger (Start, Harness, Council, Pipeline, Compare, Chat) are NOT the DOM ids in static/index.html (start, harness, hall, council, debate, chat): 'Council' is data-tab=hall and 'Pipeline' is data-tab=council, while data-tab=council is the Pipeline pane. tab_registry records the mapping and tests/test_uiux_roadmap.py fails if it drifts. Screenshot capture needs a Chrome/Chromium binary and puppeteer-core, neither vendored. Stories that claim visual evidence must capture it on a machine that has them, and must not mark visual evidence as passed when the capture was skipped.

The six panes share one shell, one integration strip and one telemetry rail. A story scoped to one pane can regress another; the feature-preservation matrix is the checklist, and P5-01..P5-03 plus P6-01/P6-02 are the regression gates.

A parallel session owns the optional M5 P6 stories (the lessons/retrieval work). If a UI story surfaces a backend defect, it is recorded as a new M5 story or an open risk, never fixed inside a UI pull request.

The program's prose had drifted from the code at the pin: the program page still said 102 routes and 11 pinned files while app.py mounts 115 and the manifest now pins 12. Counts in docs are re-derived from the artifacts, not remembered.

Every fetch( in the inline script appears as a call site; every resolved URL is classified exactly once; every exact match names a route app.py mounts for the method the call uses; a runtime-chosen segment can never be reported as exact; the three known resolution paths (literal, local const, helper call sites) are pinned; the map, manifest and ledger share one pin and one frontend digest; --check is proved to fail on a temporary copy.

Provenance: the generator and its tests are ported from arena/dc36f4b7 (PR #104), which could not merge because it conflicted with main and carried a runtime-program benchmark change. An unresolved hand-off now makes the caller list an explicit lower bound instead of a clean table. decisions: A URL segment chosen at runtime is a dynamic match with candidates, never an exact match: guessing one of two routes would turn a finding into a false statement.

A route parameter absorbs any URL segment, while a URL wildcard may only stand in for a literal route segment - that asymmetry keeps {model_id:path} routes matching without mislabelling ordinary parameter routes.
Helper URLs are resolved from call sites: consumeSSE(url, ...) has no URL of its own, and reading its name would have produced a wrong or empty row.
Routes without a browser caller are published as information, not as defects, because the CLI, the demo tour and the tests use the same API.

The story was re-done on a clean branch rather than merged from PR #104, so the runtime-program benchmark change it carried stays out of a UI/UX pull request; the generator and tests were ported rather than re-invented.

A dynamic match records its caller as possible on every candidate, never as certain on one: the literal argument at the call site is what proves which route runs, and a table that picks the first candidate invents that proof. The same rule makes 'no browser caller' a lower bound whenever any call site stays unresolved, which is why the map publishes caller_resolution.complete instead of leaving a reader to assume it.

Criterion 4 (failure and recovery states are honest): the artifact's not_verified block states exactly what it cannot prove - that a reference is a consultation and not a guard, that a blank cell means 'nothing at this depth' rather than 'unguarded', that a computed status code is recorded as dynamic instead of guessed, and that no request was sent so no refusal was observed. Criterion 5 (demonstrable by test): twelve tests re-derive the trace's claims rather than trusting them. Coverage is derived from the P0-03 map in both directions; every traced route's handler, line and decorator are re-read from app.py; the shared boundary's refusals are re-read from the middleware's own returns and its constant-time comparison is asserted; every handler refusal is matched to a real raise in that handler, with computed codes counted separately; every first-party subsystem app.py imports must carry a classification (a new module cannot slip in unclassified); the trace, route map, manifest and ledger must share one pin; and --check is proved to fail when a refusal in app.py changes, using a temporary copy.

So the tone paints the dot and the hairline and the component stays legible in greyscale, where the words carry it.

The state table gained honest tones without changing a single label. failed, error and cancelled all shared amber with paused before; failure is danger now and cancellation is neutral. tests/test_task_events.py pinned the old colour classes and now pins the tones with the words unchanged, which is what makes the vocabulary change visible as a vocabulary change rather than a rendering change.

evidence: The defect was structural, not cosmetic: nine backdrops carried role=dialog, each open function added .open and each close function removed it, Escape removed it from all nine at once, no dialog trapped focus and exactly one of the nine remembered where focus came from. A keyboard user tabbed out of an open dialog into the page behind it and, on close, landed on the document body.

There is one controller now. openOverlay(id) records the return target, paints the backdrop, sets aria-modal, makes every element sibling of the backdrop inert and focuses the first control inside after the frame that paints it; closeOverlay(id) reverses all four in one place. Because the return lives there, Escape, a Close button and a backdrop click all return focus to the same control instead of three different outcomes.

The trap is belt and braces on purpose: inert is what actually stops Tab, clicks and screen-reader traversal reaching the background, and the Tab handler is the fallback for a browser without it, wrapping the cycle inside the dialog. The walk proves the fallback matters: two full cycles of Tab past the last control never left the dialog, on all nine.

Escape closes the top overlay only, not every overlay. The old one-liner lost the stack, so a dialog opened from another dialog vanished without returning focus to the one underneath - a behaviour no screenshot would show.

Focus return has a fallback for the case that made the old code give up: a chord pressed with the page focused has no opener, so the controller remembers the last control the user actually used (focusin) and returns there rather than to nothing. This is what makes Ctrl+K then Escape land on the palette's trigger.

The shortcut situation had the same shape as the statuses did in P1-03: the rail's Alt+N lived in data-shortcut, the palette's key lived in the handler, and the palette's hints were string literals beside neither, which is how Alt+6 stayed advertised and dead until P1-02. One registry now feeds the handler, the palette rows and the markup: every rail tab gained aria-keyshortcuts, and palette rows name their shortcut by id, resolved when the list is drawn.

Two palette rows were added because the story's acceptance criterion is keyboard reachability for every dialog: Start (which had no palette row at all) and the official Harness bridge. All nine dialogs now have a keyboard path, six through the palette and three through their own controls.

The inspector was a drawer with unstated behaviour. It declares aria-modal only while it covers the page (set on open, removed on close, never the invalid 'false'), takes focus when it opens below 1100px, returns focus to its toggle when Escape closes it, and drops the modal claim on resize when it becomes a column again.

evidence: The defect was that the shell had four ways to say nothing useful and one way to say nothing at all. A refused request pasted "Error: " plus the exception message into whichever element happened to be nearby; a dropped harness event stream said nothing and retried every four seconds, so a frozen timeline and a stopped task looked identical. None of them said what was kept or what a reader could do next, which is the difference between a failure and a recovery.

The component is one shape with three kinds. empty says nothing has happened yet and what will appear; error says something failed and carries role=alert so a screen reader hears it; recovery says the state was interrupted and how it resumes. The kind sets the tone - a hairline for empty, --rose for error, --amber for recovery - and nothing else.

The cause and the what-is-kept line are required arguments, not prose a caller remembers to write. presentInto() throws 'presentation refused: ...' on an unknown kind, a blank title, cause or context, no actions, or an action whose run is not a function. The labels 'Cause: ' and 'Kept: ' are drawn by the stylesheet through ::before, so a call site supplies the sentence and cannot ship without the label.

Five live paths are wired, and each one changed behaviour rather than only appearance. Start: a failed preflight no longer replaces the checklist with one blocked row - the steps from the last successful read stay, and the presentation says nothing was changed by the attempt. Chat: the old handler appended the error to the assistant bubble and left an empty bubble behind, so a retry duplicated the message; the placeholder is now rolled back, the transcript is kept, and Retry re-sends exactly once. Harness: a dropped stream names its cause, the number of events still shown and the cursor it resumes from, and offers both Reconnect now and Reload from snapshot. evidence: The gap was not missing data, it was unused data. /api/onboarding/preflight has returned ready, blocked, completed_count, total_count and exactly one next_step since AS-039; the pane rendered six equal-weight rows, put the summary in a pill and disabled the Run button with no reason printed anywhere. A first-run reader had to read six paragraphs to find their one, and a keyboard user met a control that refused without saying why.

The pane now prints the server's answer once, above the list: '3 of 6 steps ready', 'Next: Connect a model source', that step's own detail, and the action label the preflight attached to it. The row it named carries aria-current="step" and a visible NEXT chip, so the eye and the screen reader resolve to the same row; the pill now states the verdict (Ready / Needs you / Blocked) instead of repeating the count, so a progress line has exactly one home.

A step the server gives no action is printed as following the next one rather than as a button that does nothing. first-task is action-required with no action whenever no model is selectable, and the thing to click in that state is the model step above it - which the matrix confirms is always actionable: in all 13 input combinations that produced a next step, it carried both an action token and a label.

Run stays disabled when the preflight is not ready, but the refusal is now stated twice on purpose: a visible line naming the step that is holding it up, and the same text as the button's aria-describedby. That is the ledger's invariant about disabled controls - a disabled control must reflect an authoritative refusal - made readable instead of merely true.

Two focus bugs surfaced while wiring this, both real and both fixed: clearPresentation() destroyed the button that held focus and left the reader on <body>, so it now hands focus to a caller-named target (a successful re-check returns to the lead; dismissing a chat error returns to the composer); and handing focus to the lead before rebuilding it dropped focus anyway, because the very next line replaced the focused node. The walk caught the second one after the first fix, which is why the walk reads document.activeElement rather than trusting the code.

Proof is measured in two places. scripts/uiux_onboarding_inventory.py calls the pure preflight module for 13 input combinations (auth, provider variants, local probe states, workspace, three execution modes) and fails on a next step with no action, a step with no title, a pane that recounts readiness or counts steps client-side, an invented aria-current, a missing waiting line, a Run button whose description stops naming the blocker, a clearPresentation() that drops focus, a focus hand-off to a node about to be re-rendered, or a state with no rule. scripts/start_walk.mjs reads the same response the pane read and holds the pane against it in a browser, including a refused preflight and a keyboard-pressed Re-check.

The walk records one limit honestly: this host is not ready (3 of 6), so the ready-state branch is asserted through the preflight contract and the matrix rather than by making the machine ready. Nothing in this record claims a ready journey was walked on this host.

Acceptance is the reviewer's call. This record states what was measured on this tree; the pull request is where the story is reviewed against its criteria, and the ledger does not treat its own closure as that review.
README.md was not touched: the preflight, its route and its six steps are unchanged, and the story changes how the pane presents an answer the product already gave.

evidence: The gap: Start is the pane you land on to begin work, and it could not show a single thing already done. GET /api/harness/sessions returns every session ordered by updated_at DESC, and nothing in the Start pane read it - so past work was reachable only by remembering it existed and going to the Harness.

The fix is a read, not a second store. renderStartRecent() takes the first five sessions and draws one button each: title, step count, policy and the tail of the workspace path, plus a state pill. Clicking or pressing Enter on a row switches to the Harness and selects that session - the session is opened where it lives, and Start keeps no copy of it.

Every run state the server writes has words, and Start did not invent its own. The pill is painted by harnessStatusBadge(), the table P1-03 established for all harness surfaces. The inventory reads every _update_harness_session_state(status=...) literal and the column default out of app.py and fails if the table has no row: all eight today (blocked, cancelled, completed, error, idle, paused, running, waiting_approval) map to a tone and a label.

Start owns nothing. No POST, PATCH or DELETE appears anywhere in the recent-work code: creating, retitling and deleting sessions stay in the Harness, so there is one place that owns them and one place to reason about when they change. The inventory asserts both the route list and the method list.

The launcher is a handoff, not a launch. launchTaskFromStart() writes the text into #harnessPromptInput, dispatches input so the composer's own listeners see it, focuses it and stops - it makes no request and calls nothing that runs. The workspace, the worktree decision and the execution policy are chosen in the Harness, and a run begun from a pane that cannot show them is a run begun with the wrong ones. The walk proves the claim by counting sessions and stream content before and after: unchanged.

The handoff note quotes the preflight instead of assuming success. It says ready, or not ready with the next step named, and it is refreshed whenever the preflight is re-read, so it cannot say ready an hour after the lead stopped saying it. The same text is the input's aria-describedby.

Empty and unreadable both use the P1-05 presentation component, with a cause, what is kept and an action. The unreadable one says 'nothing was changed; the task composer below still opens a task in the Harness' - which is true, and is why the error does not disable the pane. Adding startRecentState to the P1-05 container map was part of this story: that artifact exists so a new empty-or-broken container cannot be introduced without being registered.

Two of this story's own checks were wrong before they were right, and both were caught by breaking the source: the row check passed on a comment that merely named harnessStatusBadge() until it was narrowed to an assignment, and the handoff-note check passed on the word 'ready' until it was narrowed to the preflight's own verdict. A rule that can be satisfied by prose next to the code is not a rule.

Limits stated rather than papered over: the recent list is the Harness's ordering, not a notion of recency invented here; a session's step count is what the server stored; and the walk creates the session it shows, so nothing in this evidence depends on demo state it did not make itself.
Acceptance is the reviewer's call. This record states what was measured on this tree; the pull request is where the story is reviewed against its criteria.
README.md was not touched: no route, no capability and no execution path changed - Start gained a view of work that already existed and a way to hand a task to the pane that owns it.

stories.current_behavior: Recorded at P2-03. The pane that answers 'should I start here?' had no answer to 'is this machine working?'. GET /api/telemetry already reported the runtime verdict, unified memory, containers and perf, but only the telemetry rail drew it; the Start pane never read it. The page also had no second way to see which directory a task would run in: that setting lived only on the Harness pane (#harnessWorkspaceInput), read from GET /api/harness/sessions' default_workspace/git_info and written by POST /api/workspace/directory, so a reader landing on Start could begin a task - the launcher arrived in P2-02 - without ever seeing where it would run or whether the machine could run it. The demo has no model runtime, so /api/telemetry answers with _demo_telemetry_payload() and telemetry_source='simulated_demo' there: a surface that rendered those numbers plainly would present the demo's figures as this machine's.
stories.target_behavior: Start shows a System health card and a Project workspace card. The health card draws four rows - model runtime, unified memory (used/total plus the oMLX cap), containers, and the project workspace - from the payload renderTelemetry() already fetched, so it never polls and the card and the rail cannot disagree; every value comes out of that payload; and the evidence line states the basis: measured when a runtime answered, unverified plus a Demo data pill when the payload is simulated, unavailable when nothing answered. In the simulated and unavailable cases the claim says which rows still describe this machine (the workspace row, which comes from the session list). The workspace card names the configured directory and its git state, writes through the Harness's own saveWorkspaceDirectory()/POST /api/workspace/directory, re-reads the preflight afterwards, and presents a refusal with its cause, the directory still in force, and Retry.

evidence: The gap was a read nobody did. GET /api/telemetry (app.py) has reported omlx_online, memory, omlx.ceiling_gb, models and docker since the rail was built, and the Start pane drew none of it; the workspace lived only on the Harness pane. Both answers existed; neither was where a reader starts.

One payload, two surfaces. renderTelemetry() now stores the payload it just read in lastTelemetry and the card renders that; the inventory fails if the card contains a fetch( of its own, if renderTelemetry() stops feeding it, or if a failed read leaves the old payload in place. There is still exactly one poll loop.

Nothing is invented. The memory row is memory.omlx_gb + orbstack_gb + macos_apps_gb over total_gb with omlx.ceiling_gb as the cap, the container row is docker.containers.length with orbstack_detected, the runtime row is omlx_online, and the workspace row is default_workspace. The read time is the pane's own Date.now(): the payload has no timestamp, and the first draft's d.read_at was caught by the inventory's invented-field rule before it shipped.

The demo is labelled, not trusted. This host has no model runtime, so /api/telemetry returned telemetry_source='simulated_demo' and the walk (not the author) observed it: pill Demo data, basis unverified, claim 'no model runtime answered, so the runtime and memory rows are the demo payload and describe no machine. The workspace row is still this machine's'. The measured branch is asserted structurally by the inventory and by the same walk on a host that has a runtime.

The card keeps its shape when it cannot read. The first draft dropped the memory and container rows when there was no payload; the walk caught that two rows, not three, said 'not measured yet'. A row that disappears reads as 'that part is fine', so all four rows now persist and say they do not know, and the absent_keeps_shape rule fails if that regresses.

A failed read is actionable. Basis unavailable alone left the reader nothing to press, so the card presents an error naming GET /api/telemetry, saying the workspace row is unaffected and why, and offering Re-check and Monitor rail - while the footer buttons hide, so the same two controls are not printed twice in one card.

The workspace is one setting, written one way. saveStartWorkspace() calls saveWorkspaceDirectory(), the handler the Harness already uses, which now returns { ok, dir, recent, git } instead of only toasting; startWorkspaceInput joined syncProjectDirInputs() so the two panes cannot point at different directories. The walk proved it end to end: row, server default_workspace and #harnessWorkspaceInput all changed together and all came back.

A change is followed by a fresh preflight. After a successful write the pane re-reads /api/onboarding/preflight (the walk counted the requests: 2 -> 4) and the workspace step reports ready for the new directory. A checklist that keeps saying the workspace is unwritable after it was set is worse than no checklist.

A refusal says what is still true. With POST /api/workspace/directory aborted the pane presented 'The workspace was not changed / Cause: Failed to fetch / Kept: <dir> is still the project directory; nothing was created or moved' with Retry and Open Harness, the row still showed the old directory, and the server still reported it. Pressing Retry with Enter performed the write the route had refused.

Failures were photographed, not described. The walk frames each capture on its subject (startWorkspaceState, startHealthState) after a first attempt showed a toast and the fold above the card - the picture has to show the thing being judged.

The walk restores the workspace in a finally block over HTTP, so a crash mid-walk cannot leave the demo pointing at a scratch directory; its own scratch capture is named health-narrow.png because narrow.png belongs to P2-01 and a second walk silently overwriting it would make that picture describe a pane it never showed.

The basis is chosen from the payload, not from optimism. A simulated payload is a real state the demo tour produces on every run, so rendering it plainly would be the most common lie in the product.

Changing the workspace re-reads the preflight rather than patching the checklist locally. The server owns readiness; the pane's job is to ask again.
A refused write names the directory still in force. 'It failed' leaves the reader unsure whether their project moved; the interesting fact is that nothing did.

The demo's simulated numbers are not hidden from the capture. The screenshots show DEMO DATA because that is the honest state of this host, and a picture of a healthier machine would be documenting a machine nobody ran.

stories.description: Incrementally implement chat composer and conversation hierarchy using current code as authoritative baseline.
stories.current_behavior: Recorded at P2-04. The Chat pane could send and stream, but it named nobody and promised the wrong thing. renderChatMessages() drew a bare .msg per turn: an answer's model lived in a .msg-meta footer *under* the answer, a question carried no label at all, nothing numbered the turns, and the function ended with `box.scrollTop = box.scrollHeight`, so the pane dragged the reader to the bottom on every token - reading back through a long reply was a fight with the stream. The composer said "(Enter to send)" in its placeholder, which was true, and then sent whatever #chatModel held including an empty string, leaving /api/chat/stream to explain; the Send button was enabled in states that could not work and gave no reason when it failed. The tools checkbox explained nothing at all: /api/chat/stream runs the turn under policy 'plan' (read-only) and falls back to WORKSPACE_ROOT when no directory is sent. Clear wiped chatHistory and drew "Session cleared." - one stray click from a long conversation the server cannot give back.
stories.target_behavior: Every turn carries its role, its number and - for an answer - the model that produced it, above the content, from one CHAT_ROLES table; the transcript is role=log with aria-live=off and aria-busy while streaming, follows the stream only when the reader was already within CHAT_PIN_SLACK of the bottom, and otherwise keeps the position and offers Jump to latest (which moves scroll and focus together). One predicate, chatSendReason(), decides whether the composer can send; the disabled button and the sentence under it both read it, and the sentence is a live region rewritten only when its reason or the model changes. The reasons are: streaming, no-model, runtime-offline (read from the telemetry verdict, local models only, worded as what the probe reported), tools-readonly (naming the directory it would read and the 'plan' policy), and ready (saying what Enter does). Clear keeps the turns it removes and presents Undo; Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line, in one handler, matching the placeholder.

evidence: The transcript named nobody. A reply's model was a footer under the reply, a question had no label, and nothing numbered the turns, so 'which answer is this?' was a scroll rather than a glance. CHAT_ROLES now gives every role a label and a tone in one table, and each turn prints data-role, the label, the model (answers) and its index.

The pane fought the reader. renderChatMessages() ended with an unconditional scrollTop assignment; every streamed token yanked the view to the bottom. It now measures chatNearBottom() before re-rendering, follows only if the reader was already there, and shows Jump to latest otherwise - the walk proves it by scrolling to the top and appending a turn (scrollTop 0 -> 0, jump visible).

The transcript is a log, not a live region. role=log with aria-live=off and aria-busy while streaming: the pane re-renders on every token, and a live region there would read the whole conversation aloud repeatedly. What is announced is the composer's reason, which changes only when the answer to 'can I send?' changes.

The composer had no single answer. It promised Enter-to-send and then sent an empty model id when #chatModel held nothing. chatSendReason() is now the only predicate: the disabled button and the sentence both read it, and the walk proves that a blocked Send returns without sending, focuses the composer, and says why.

The hint is written once per answer. The kind of live region that announces 'no model selected' on every token is worse than no live region, so the text is rewritten only when its reason or the model changes (chatHintSignature).

The reasons are ranked by what a reader needs first. The first draft put the tools note above the runtime verdict; on this host the probe says the runtime is not answering, so the composer told the reader about read-only tools while the send was about to fail. runtime-offline now precedes tools-readonly.

The runtime warning is a report, not a prophecy. The first wording was 'will probably fail' - and the demo then answered from its scripted runtime directly above it. It now says what the telemetry probe reported and what happens if it is right (the message is kept, Retry is offered).

The tools note describes the route. /api/chat/stream runs the turn under policy 'plan' and falls back to WORKSPACE_ROOT when no directory is sent, so the sentence says read-only and names the directory - the first draft claimed the tools 'will refuse', a failure the server does not produce. The inventory fails if the policy literal in app.py changes.

Clear is undoable. clearChat() keeps the turns it removes and presents the recovery kind with Undo, and Clear is disabled when the transcript is empty. The walk clears, reads the count in the presentation, presses Undo with the keyboard, and gets every turn back with the cursor in the composer.

Enter sends, Shift+Enter does not, in one handler. The rule is scoped to the chat handler specifically: three other composers on the shell bind Enter too, and a rule that read the whole file would be satisfied by any of them.

A real send works end to end. The demo replays a scripted reply, so the walk types a message, presses Enter, and checks the answer's label, its model header and its tok/s meta, plus the composer returning to idle with Stop hidden and the field cleared. The failure surface is reached by refusing POST /api/chat/stream: error kind, cause 'Failed to fetch', the message kept, the empty placeholder rolled back so Retry sends one message and not two.

Two shared defects surfaced because the artifacts caught them lying. uiux_route_map._brace_end() treated the apostrophe in a comment as an opening quote, so one comment stretched a function's body across the file: stopActiveStream inherited every call after it and the sign-off attributed Council's /api/hall/sessions/{id}/summon to Chat and Pipeline. The scanner now skips // and /* */ comments, and the sign-off attributes that route to Council alone. Separately, the P1-05 negative test unwired only the first presentInto("chatState"), which stopped being a hole once Clear got its own; it now unwires every call site.
The acceptance criteria are the reviewer's call. This story records what was run and what was seen; the artifacts prove freshness, not owner review (issue #126).

stories.agent_prompt: Implement UIUX-P2-05 (Chat model context streaming and tool transparency). Verify dependencies, pin HEAD, inventory impacted controls and API routes, preserve all current behavior, make a small compatible change, execute targeted and baseline tests, record screenshots, and mark done only with passing evidence. Never invent a test result.

evidence: A reply was the product of a request the pane never showed. #chatModel, #chatReasoning, the tools checkbox, the active skill set and the message list all went to POST /api/chat/stream, and none of it was printed, so "why did it answer like that?" had no answer in the pane. chatContextSnapshot() is now called once, when the request is built, stored on the turn as m.context, and printed as "Context: model <id> · <persona> · reasoning <mode> · tools on (read-only)|tools off · N skills · N messages sent · <directory>". Recomputing it at render time would describe the composer as it is now, not the request that went out, so the inventory fails on any chatContextSnapshot() call inside renderChatMessages().

Two different facts were being collapsed into one. The workspace field is usually empty, and the server then reads WORKSPACE_ROOT. Printing only what was sent would leave the reader guessing which directory the tools touched; printing only the effective one would hide that nothing was sent. The snapshot carries workspace (literally sent, possibly "") and workspace_effective (what the server will read), and the walk proves both: a written turn shows "the configured default project directory", and a real send records workspace "/tmp/m5-demo-.../workspace" -> reads the same path.

The line leads with the model because the turn header names the model that answered. They agree today; if the server ever falls back they would not, and the context line is the record of what was asked for.

A tool call was a border colour and 72 characters of JSON. app.py yields chat_tool with step, tool, args, ok, elapsed_ms and a preview capped at 500 characters; the pane drew a tinted box and JSON.stringify(t.args).slice(0,72), so the rest of the arguments was unreachable and a failed call looked like a slightly redder successful one. Each row now prints a status word (OK/FAILED) with a tone, data-tool-status, the tool, "step N · N ms · N B of arguments", and a disclosure holding the whole argument object and the output, labelled with the server cap.
The summary is the part a reader who opens nothing sees. "2 tool calls · 1 failed · 127 ms" is computed from the same list the rows are drawn from, so the count and the rows cannot disagree.

The streaming clock is measured and it stops. sendChatRequest() records timing.startedAt before the fetch and stamps firstTokenAt inside the token() handler; the finished turn freezes endedAt in done(). Before a token arrives the turn says "waiting for the first token" rather than a zero. There is no timer: the numbers are a snapshot per render, which is why they freeze instead of ticking, and the page says so.

Two rules the first draft got wrong, caught by the walk rather than by review. A turn drawn with no usage but no send flag read aria-busy="false", so the transcript announced itself idle while an answer was arriving: busy now follows chatHistory.some(m => m.role === "assistant" && !m.usage) as well as the pane's own flag. And the context line omitted the model while claiming to record the request: the walk asserts the model appears before any other field.

The pane and the route are checked against each other. The inventory reads the chat_tool dict out of app.py and the preview cap, and fails if the pane reads a field the route does not send (tool.duration_ms, in the negative test), if the route stops sending elapsed_ms, or if the cap changes while the pane still says 500.

The walk writes what it cannot stream. This host has no model runtime, so scripts/chat_context_walk.mjs writes one turn of the shape sendChatRequest() builds - a passing and a failing tool call, both timings, a reasoning trace - and holds the pane against it byte for byte (arguments 45 B and 35 B, elapsed 120 ms and 7 ms, summary 127 ms), then shows a turn before its first token, then sends one real message and checks the context recorded on that turn against the composer it was sent from.

The four captures are the pipeline's, not hand-made: this environment has no system browser, so they were taken with Chromium 153 from the npm package @sparticuz/chromium (its al2023 NSS layer) driven by puppeteer-core 23, through scripts/chat_context_walk.mjs --screenshots docs/media/chat.

The acceptance criteria are the reviewer's call. This story records what was run and what was seen; the artifacts prove freshness, not owner review (issue #126 still reports historical-approval-unbound, which is the owner's to resolve).

Two workspace fields instead of one sentence. What was sent and what will be read are different facts, and a line that prints only one of them is either misleading or empty.

The model leads the context line even though the header already names the model: the header names the model that answered, the line records the model that was asked, and a copied line has to stand on its own.
Status is a word with a tone, never a colour. Colour alone is not a status for a reader who cannot see it, and a failed call must not look like a successful one that is slightly redder.
The summary, not the disclosures, is the contract with a reader in a hurry: it counts calls, failures and milliseconds from the list the rows are drawn from.

The clock is measured and frozen, with no timer. A number that keeps moving without a render is invented, and a turn that keeps counting after its stream stopped is wrong; the page states that the figures freeze when nothing is arriving.
busy follows a turn without usage, not only the pane's send flag: the first draft announced an arriving answer as idle, which the walk caught.

The walk writes a turn for the tool cases and sends one real message. The demo has no model runtime, so the tool calls cannot be provoked; the written turn uses the same helpers and shape the live path uses, and the real send proves the context line on an actual request. evidence: There was no crossing between Chat and the Harness. A conversation that turned into work had to be retyped, and the record of what the model was told, which tools ran and which failed stayed in the pane that is least able to act on it. The Chat transcript bar now carries one control - Open in Harness - whose sentence and disabled state come from a single predicate, chatHandoffReason(), exactly as chatSendReason() does for Send.

The handoff is a carry, not a request. handOffChatToHarness() reads the turns the pane already holds, writes a brief into the Harness composer and stops: no fetch, no EventSource, no run call, no chatHistory = []. The walk records every request the page makes while it presses the button and asserts that none of them is a write and none is a read the two panes do not already perform (the only traffic is the telemetry poll and the Harness's own session list, both GETs from switchTab).

The brief reports the turns instead of summarising them: the last user task, the message and reply counts, the tool-call and failure counts, the P2-05 context line recorded on the last reply, and each of the last eight tool calls with its status word, step, time and output - clipped at 200 characters, with the clip and the server's own 500-character cap stated in the brief itself, plus a pointer to the transcript for the rest.

The Harness stays the admission surface. The brief is text in the composer; the workspace, the workflow mode, the policy and the approvals are still chosen there, and Run is still the only thing that starts anything. The story adds no route: the inventory fails if the handler names an /api/harness path or if a /api/chat/handoff endpoint ever appears in app.py.

The receipt is what makes the leaving honest. The Chat pane presents a recovery with the counts it carried, that nothing has run, that the transcript is kept, and Back to Chat / Open Harness. Back to Chat dismisses the receipt and focuses the composer unconditionally - the first version leaned on clearPresentation's "only if the receipt had focus" rule and left the cursor on <body>, which the walk caught.

The pane remembers what it handed over with chatHandoffMark, so the sentence becomes "Already in the Harness composer (2 messages, 10 tool calls); nothing has run." instead of offering the same carry again. Clear and Undo reset the mark, and so does a failed attempt: the walk showed a failure leaving the sentence claiming a carry that had not happened, which is two claims and one lie.

The failure path is reachable and honest. The walk removes #harnessPromptInput from the page, presses the button, and gets an error named "The handoff did not happen" with its cause, the line that the conversation and its tool calls are untouched, and Retry / Dismiss; restoring the composer and pressing Retry performs the handoff. Nothing is cleared and no state is invented.

The sentence was shortened to fit one line: the first wording ran to 130 characters and was ellipsized in the bar at 1440px, which is a status line nobody finishes. It now reads "Carries 2 messages (1 reply) and 10 tool calls (1 failed) to the Harness; nothing runs there." and the walk asserts it fits on one line at 900px.

A P1-05 negative test had silently stopped being a hole. test_a_raw_writer_in_a_converted_handler_is_caught injected its raw writer after the bare substring `    clearPresentation("chatState");`, and the new Back to Chat action contains that string at a deeper indent, so str.replace put the injection inside handOffChatToHarness - not a wired handler - and the rule had nothing to report. The test is now anchored inside sendChatRequest with a text.count(marker) == 1 guard, which is the general lesson: a negative test must prove where it landed, not just that it changed something.

evidence: Nine controls decided a Harness run and none of them said what the run would do with them, and "can this run?" had three answers: a toast in the GSD path, a different toast in the SDLC path, and a silent `return` in the turn path. The composer now prints the plan above Run - `directory` (plus `direct` or `isolated git worktree`), `policy`, `models` (lead, then the critic or `same`), `workflow` (the mode with the three advanced settings it depends on, and `N changed` in words) - and every value is read from the control the run payload posts.

The plan covers the payload by construction, and the inventory enforces it from both ends: `ids_in_the_payload` is parsed out of the `consumeSSE("/api/harness/run", {...})` and `/api/harness/gsd-wave` payload objects, `ids_the_plan_reads` is parsed out of `harnessRunPlan()` (plus the `HARNESS_ADVANCED_IDS` list it iterates), and `covers_the_run_payload` fails when a control is added to the payload without being added to the plan. `watches_the_same_controls` fails when the change listeners and the payload diverge, so the plan cannot go stale against a control it is not watching.

The policy is printed as the option's own label. The first version of the row appended a description from a `HARNESS_POLICY_EFFECT` table and read "Standard (Ask before Bash) - asks before Bash"; the table was deleted, the row now prints `harnessSelectedText("harnessPolicy")`, and `policy_is_the_option_label` fails if a second description of a policy appears anywhere in the file. One string, so the sentence a reader sees cannot drift from the option they chose.

The three settings that used to hide inside `<details id="harnessAdvanced">` now state their own contents while the group is closed: the summary reads `Ponytail + Concise · Low · 10 steps`, and appends `· changed` when one differs from the `data-default` its own markup declares. `declared_default_is_the_selected_option` pins each declared default to the option the markup ships selected, so a fresh pane cannot open marked as changed, and `changed_is_marked_in_words` keeps the word - colour is reinforcement, never the status.

`harnessRunState()` is one predicate for Run, exactly as `chatSendReason()` is for Send: `updateHarnessRunControl()` sets `button.disabled = !state.ready` and writes the same answer into a polite live region that the composer points at with `aria-describedby`. The reasons are `running`, `board`, `no-task` and `ready`; the board mode needs no task because opening the SDLC board runs nothing, and the inventory fails if that exception is lost.

Two real defects closed with that predicate. `executeHarnessSelectedWorkflow()` now consults it before dispatching, so an empty task is the sentence beside Run rather than a silent `return` (the GSD and SDLC paths keep their own guards for their own buttons); and because `harnessRunActive` is the first branch, Enter in a busy composer can no longer start a second stream - before this story `runHarnessTurn()` set the button's `disabled` but the keydown handler called the dispatcher directly. `setHarnessRunActive()` re-evaluates on both edges, so a finished run leaves an empty box and Run off rather than enabled and inert.

The pane now answers the brief UIUX-P2-06 carries. `handOffChatToHarness()` records what it carried, and a banner that starts hidden appears with the counts (`2 messages, 2 tool calls (1 failed)`), the model and the effective directory the reply was sent with, and the difference: `This run changes 2 settings: the model (demo-local-model -> combo/hybrid-resilient); the project directory (/tmp/chat-read-project -> /tmp/p3-01-walk-project)`. It keeps comparing as controls change, says `This run uses the same model and project directory it was read with` when nothing differs, writes only when the sentence changes, and goes when the task goes - a run consumes it, **+ New session** clears it, and emptying the composer clears it.

The task box grows with the task. A carried brief arrived in a two-row textarea that showed its first two lines and hid the rest, including the sentence that nothing had run; `fitHarnessComposer()` sizes the box to its content between a two-row floor and a ten-row ceiling, follows the reader as they type, and returns it to rest when a run takes the task away. Manual resizing stays off (`resize:none`) so a drag cannot fight the fitter - the walk measures both the growth and the rest.

Accessibility, found by walking the pane rather than assuming it: the four `<label>`s naming the lead model, the critic, the execution policy and the max steps had no `for`, so those selects had no accessible name, and the task box had no name at all. All four labels are associated, the composer carries `aria-label="Your task for the Harness"` and `aria-describedby="harnessRunHint"`, and the inventory fails on any of the ten controls in the bar and composer that carries no visible text of its own and no label or `aria-label`.

Nothing that worked stopped working: eleven controls in the bar, the sidebar and the composer are pinned to the handler or binding that made each work (`PRESERVED_CONTROLS`), and the five routes they write through (`POST /api/workspace/directory`, `PATCH /api/harness/sessions/{id}`, `POST /api/harness/run`, `/gsd-wave`, `/sdlc/run`) are checked to be still mounted in `app.py`. No route was added: the plan reads state that is already in the pane and writes nothing.

stories.current_behavior: The server has always written a durable event log and served it from a cursor, and the pane kept it to itself. Its trajectory renderer had a card for 18 of the 43 event types app.py emits and returned an empty string for the other 25 - session/init (so every session began blank), all seven security/* types (so a policy change left no trace) and the whole edit/*, delegation/*, handoff/* and mcp/* families - so a session with a real log drew an empty trajectory. renderStoredHarnessEvents() rewrote the whole transcript on every frame and then set scrollTop = scrollHeight, pulling a reader who had scrolled up back to the bottom, and nothing stated the cursor, how many events were held, or whether the view came from the stream, a re-read or a snapshot. Resync existed but only as a toast.
stories.target_behavior: The trajectory states what it is a view of, and a reader can rebuild it from the record. A strip above the trajectory states the count, the seq range, the cursor and how the view was filled (following the stream, a page read, a snapshot the log would not resume from), and opens into one row per held event, oldest first, each row a button that brings its card into view and marks it. Every retained event draws, so the cards a reader counts equal the events the log holds. Replay re-reads the log from its first retained event and rebuilds the view from it, refusing to report success on a gap. A frame that lands while the reader is scrolled up does not move them and does not shut the cards they opened; Jump to latest, offered only when they are away from the newest event, is the only control that scrolls them.

`renderStoredHarnessEventHtml()` now ends in `renderRecordedHarnessEventHtml(ev)`, so a type with no card arrives as a compact line read from the event (`session/init  standard policy · direct /tmp/... · lead Qwen3.8-27B`, `security/policy_revision  standard -> plan (revision 2)`, `edit/applied  applied · src/app.py`). The inventory fails on `renderer_ends_in_the_fallback`, on any `return ""` in the renderer, and on a card for a type nothing emits (`no_dead_branches`) - a dead branch is a card no event can reach.

The strip states what the trajectory is: `following the log from seq 13 · 13 events held · replayed 3 times` while the stream fills it, `1 event held, seq 1-1 · cursor 1 of 1` after a page read with the stream closed, `the log did not resume (events_pruned), so this view is the snapshot's: task state and 9 events, seq 5-13` when the fallback fired, and `· 4 earlier events pruned, retained from seq 5 · this view holds 9 of the 13 events last reported` for a pruned or incomplete view. Every one of those sentences is produced by harnessLogState() from the log it holds and the last page it read, not from prose; the walk reads each one out of the DOM.

The reader's place survives a frame. `harnessStreamNearBottom()` (28px slack, the chat transcript's rule) is consulted once before the transcript is rewritten: a pinned view follows, and a reading view keeps its `scrollTop` and its open `<details>` cards - the walk scrolls to 0, replays, and reads `scrollTop 0 -> 0`. Jump to latest is drawn only when the reader is away from the newest event (`hidden at bottom=true shown when up=true`), and pressing it is what returns them (`hidden after=true atBottom=true`). The walk asks the browser for pixels, not for the `hidden` property, because `.btn` sets its own display and had made the first version of the button always visible.

Replay rebuilds from the record: `replayHarnessLog()` empties the cache, re-reads the log from its first retained event and re-renders from what came back - `before=13 after=13 cards=13`, twice, with `replayed 1 time` then `replayed 2 times`, so a replay is countable and a duplicate is impossible (the seq-keyed merge is untouched). A replay that hits a gap does not pretend: it records the reason, says so, and resyncs the authoritative snapshot instead.

The engine underneath is unchanged: the six gap reasons (no_page, snapshot_required, cursor_ahead, events_pruned, sequence_gap, missing_events), seq-deduplication, the cursor, snapshot_required handling, the pruned-history notice, the three stream frames (task_event, resync_required, stream_error) and the resync path that re-reads /state and re-anchors the stream all still work, and the inventory fails if any of them goes. No endpoint was added: the strip reads the four routes the pane already had.

The strip is capped at 45% of the pane and its list at min(168px, 22vh), and it does not shrink away: at 1440x560 the walk measures the strip keeping its line and the trajectory keeping its floor. The hidden Jump button is not drawn either - a `[hidden]` rule for `.btn` inside the strip, because `.btn`'s own display beat the UA rule and the first build showed a control that was not offered.

The card states what the click records, in the units the store uses: tool, exact arguments, capability (`scoped_grants.resolve_tool_capabilities()`), resource, and `one use · 10 minutes after you decide`. The capability line is a client table that this story's inventory imports the real function to check - 18 tools and the `mcp__*` rule - so the copy is verified rather than trusted, and the ttl it prints is compared with `SG_DEFAULT_GRANT_TTL_SECONDS`. The resource line names the path argument it can see and says where the server will resolve it; the surface prints the canonical `path:<worktree>:<rel>` from the record, so the pane never invents a scope it did not receive.

The old streamed card posted `activeHarnessId` and the workflow cards posted `d.session_id`, which is how a stale card could earn a 403. Every path now passes the session it drew with, `resolveHarnessApproval()` falls back to the selected session only when the card carried none, and the walk captures the `POST /api/harness/approve` body to prove `session_id` is the seeded session.

Expiry is stated while the offer is live: the card counts down from the request (`expires in 9 min`, then seconds), one interval drives every live card and clears itself when the last one is gone, and an offer whose slot is gone reads `Expired — re-run the turn` with `Re-run the turn to reach the gate again` - not as a refusal, because nothing was refused. The permissions surface (`#harnessGrantsModal`, opened by `#harnessPermissionBadge` in the session strip and by `Permissions & Revocations` in the session actions) lists what the session holds with tool, capability, canonical resource, limit, expiry, `issued_by` and note; the revocation rules that refuse matching actions; the history of grants that ended and how; and the approvals still waiting (with a link to the card) or expired. evidence: A verdict used to be a label. `turn/verified` drew `Completion verified (spec_sha256…)` - the digest of a contract the reader could not see - and `turn/verification_failed` drew a failure code and a reason, while the transcript, the exit code, the revision, the classification and the acceptance coverage that decided it stayed in the log. A third outcome, `turn/stagnation_paused`, was not drawn as a verdict at all. `renderHarnessVerdictCardHtml()` now draws all three from the report the runtime persisted (`TaskVerificationReport.to_dict()` is the event payload): the contract digest, the command with its exit code and classification, the revision the result is tied to and whether it moved, the modified files, the patch digest, the environment, the failing tests with their kind, the covered and uncovered criteria, and the output behind a disclosure. The inventory fails if a second verdict renderer appears or the one-line label comes back.

The card never invents a value the record does not hold: a report with no captured revision says `no revision captured`, one whose command never executed says `the verification command never ran`, and the card ends with `A verdict is the runtime's record of one turn: this card draws it, and re-runs nothing`. The inventory breaks both fallbacks in a copy of the source to prove they are checked.

The record behind the card is `#harnessEvidenceModal`, reached from the session actions (`Verification & Artifacts`), the command palette, every verdict card and the diff dialog. It reads only routes that already existed - `GET …/task` and `GET …/diff` - and draws six sections: the verdict (code, facts, failures, evidence refs, transcript digest, output), the contract (command, first stage, required output markers, required and modified files, protected digests, baseline digests, the rules in force, known failures, declared criteria), the observation (exit code, classification, pre-existing failures classified as pre-existing, output digest, and the coverage the transcript actually demonstrated), the change (branch, status, per-file +n/-m), the artifacts (checkpoints, the latest checkpoint's evidence refs, the artifact lineage, the revision a re-run would be tied to), and four statements of what the surface does not prove. No endpoint was added; the inventory fails on an invented or unmounted verification route.

Coverage is drawn as what the transcript printed, not as what the contract hoped: `evaluate_acceptance_coverage()` counts a test id only when it appears in the output and is not among the classified failures, so an uncovered criterion is drawn `NOT COVERED` and counted (`1 declared criterion(s) were not covered by an observed test`). The contract section draws the same criteria as `declared` with no verdict mark, because the contract is the gate and the observation is what happened when it was applied - a first pass drew them as uncovered there and the walk caught the contradiction.

Three absences are drawn as absences, proved in the walk: no verdict in the log (`No verdict is recorded in this session's log yet`), no contract on the session (`This session has no verification contract, so completion was not gated by one`), and an unreadable diff (`The workspace diff could not be read`). None is drawn as a pass; the walk selects a seeded session that has a contract and no verdict and asserts both that no card is drawn and that the record's verdict block carries no tone.

The change is counted once. `harnessDiffFiles()` parses the unified diff, skipping `diff --git`, `+++`, `---` and `@@` so a hunk header cannot be read as an addition, and both the record and `#harnessDiffModal` count with it - the dialog now shows `1 file(s) · +1 −1 · on master` above the diff and says `This is the worktree as it is now. It is not frozen at any verdict`. The parser is exercised against output real `git` produced in a temporary repository, not a hand-written sample.

The fixture cannot fake a verdict: only `TaskStateMachine.verify_task_completion()` produces a report, and the demo has no model runtime. `scripts/harness_evidence_seed.py` therefore builds two git workspaces, sets a real `TaskVerificationSpec` on each session, and lets that verifier decide - one workspace passes its test, one fails it - then appends the reports with `_append_harness_event()`, the writer a turn uses, and records a checkpoint with the store's own `save_checkpoint()`. What is staged is the `turn/start` and `turn/end` bookends; the revision, environment, exit code, transcript digest, classified failures and coverage are the verifier's.

A worker that died left the task saying `running` with no stream attached, and the pane drew that as a running task.

`#harnessRecoveryPanel` sits under the session strip and above the durable log, and is one presentation - so it cannot be drawn without a cause and a `Kept:` line - over a facts list and a live note. It reads only what the server already returns: `GET …/state` (status, transitions, checkpoints, budget, turns) and `GET …/task` (task record, recovery memory, containment store, budget). Every fact on it is one of those fields. No route was added.

Seven states, each with its own story: paused at a safe boundary (the transition's own reason, printed beside a plain phrase, and the checkpoint a resume restarts from); failed (with the requirement for changed evidence); blocked (the unresolved action by id, resume refused, cancel offered); cancelled (what was fenced and revoked, and that no resume exists); running and owned by this pane (a pause lands at the next safe boundary); running and not owned by this pane (the record cannot tell another tab's run from a dead worker, and the surface says so instead of guessing); and a resume the runtime accepted, drawn as `prepared` with `nothing has run yet` rather than as progress. A completed task draws no surface at all.

The presses are the real routes: Pause (`POST …/pause`, and a deferred pause says it is deferred), Resume (`POST …/resume`), Continue (`/api/harness/run` with `resume: true`, only after an accepted resume), Cancel (`POST …/cancel`, behind a confirmation that any other action disarms), Abort (the existing `/abort`, which now says it ends the view and not the work) and Start a new session. A press that reaches the server prints the answer it got - including the string `detail` a rejected transition carries and the `{code, message}` a rejected handoff carries.

Every reason a resume would be refused is computed from the same record before the press - the task state, a failed checkpoint integrity check, unresolved consequential actions, a persisted barrier, a pending cancellation, an exhausted budget, a quarantine, unreadable recovery memory - and the action stays visible and disabled with the reason as its accessible description and the same reason in text (`Not available here — …`). `presentInto()` grew `disabled`, `reason` and a `tone` for destructive actions so a refusal could be drawn instead of hidden.

The three recovery events are one card renderer now, saying what the event did (`0 in-flight process(es) were contained`, `2 consequential action(s) were left unresolved …`) and linking back to the surface that keeps saying it after the log scrolls past.

The one capability the pane could never exercise even with the routes reachable: `/api/harness/run` accepts `resume` and the pane never sent it, so a resume the runtime had accepted was followed by a turn that started over at step 1. The request now carries the flag when a resume is prepared, and consumes the preparation in that request.

`scripts/uiux_harness_recovery_inventory.py`: 44 checks over the markup, the seven stories, the six actions, the eleven refusals, the three event cards, the escaping of every value the record supplies and the seven server contracts this story had to preserve (pause's `deferred_to_safe_boundary`, cancel's `unresolved_action_ids`/`contained_processes`, resume's `ready_to_resume`/`next_step`, containment's quarantine and barrier holds, `/task`'s recovery and containment, `/state`'s `task_status` and `transitions`, and the absence of any new recovery route). 0 findings.

`scripts/harness_recovery_walk.mjs`: 23/23 checks in a real browser against `scripts/harness_recovery_seed.py`, which drives `ensure_root_task`, `transition_task`, `save_checkpoint`, `request_pause`, `cancel_task` and a real `persist_barrier_hold()` into paused / blocked / cancelled / was-running states, then presses the pane's own controls against the real routes. It proves the prepared-resume answer, the two-press cancel, the disabled refusal, that the server's own 409 agrees with the reason the surface stated, that a reason which is markup is drawn as text (no element, no handler), that focus survives an action, that a run started after a prepared resume sends `resume: true`, and that every request the surface made was one of the four routes that already existed. No page error.

evidence: The four seats are a chain - the architect writes a spec, the builder is handed it, the critic is handed both, the judge is handed all three - and that chain lived only in `api_council_stream`'s input lambdas. The pane drew four cards carrying a state and a tok/s, so a finished run could not answer the two questions a pipeline raises: what did each seat receive, and what did it hand on? A seat that produced nothing looked exactly like a seat that had just started, and a run that was stopped looked like a run that was still going.

Every stage card now carries two rows. The handoff row names what the seat reads (`the task + the Architect's spec and the Builder's draft`), the characters of upstream output it was handed, and the seat it feeds (or `ends the run` for the judge); the artifact row states what it produced - characters, tokens, tok/s, the reasoning it kept - or `produced nothing` with the empty section the next seat was handed. The collapsed step card carries its seat's character count, and `#councilArtifacts` above the cards is one live run line: how many seats finished, the total output, the handoffs that carried content forward, and whether the server saved the run.

The chain is mirrored in `PIPELINE_SEATS` and checked against `app.py` on every inventory run: the pane's copy is compared with the `c['...']` reads in each stage's input lambda, so a mirror that drifts is a failing check rather than a quiet lie.

What the surface refuses to claim is stated on it. The sizes count this pane's own stream, not the prompt the server assembles around them, and the page says so. `save_run()` is called after the fourth seat returns and returns `0` when it cannot write, so a stopped pipeline is drawn as stopped and is never given a run id; a run that finished without one says its artifacts exist only on this screen. No endpoint was added to read a saved run back: `/api/runs` does not exist and this story did not create it.

The empty seat was staged, not invented: `scripts/pipeline_artifacts_seed.py` wraps the server's own `stream_any_model` so one model arrives with usage and no content and another streams slowly enough to Stop. The events, the character counts and the run id are the server's answers.
